title: Can we achieve multiple inheritance in Java, why is multiple class inheritance disallowed (the diamond problem), and how do interfaces work around it?
keyPoints: Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class, preventing the diamond problem
Diamond problem: if A and B both override a method from C, which version does X (extending both) inherit?
Java allows multiple interface implementation: class X implements A, B is valid
If two interfaces have conflicting default methods, the implementing class must override to resolve explicitly
Resolution priority: class method wins over interface default; sub-interface default wins over super-interface default
InterfaceName.super.method() syntax lets the class delegate to a specific interface's default method

s1_definition.oneliner: No multiple class inheritance (diamond problem: ambiguous method resolution). Yes, multiple interface implementation. If two interfaces have the same default method, the implementing class must override to resolve the conflict explicitly.
s1_definition.profdef:
Java does not allow a class to extend more than one class to prevent the diamond problem.

- **Diamond problem**: if class A and class B both override a method from class C, and class X extends both A and B, the compiler cannot decide which version X inherits.
- **Java's solution**: a class can implement multiple interfaces. If both interfaces have abstract methods with the same signature, the class provides one implementation satisfying both.
- **Default method conflict**: if two interfaces provide the same default method, the compiler forces the class to override and explicitly resolve the conflict.
- **Resolution priority**: class method always wins over interface defaults. Sub-interface default wins over super-interface default.
- **Delegation syntax**: `InterfaceName.super.method()` lets the implementing class call a specific interface's default method.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Rajesh at National Bank of India works in both Trading and Compliance. Both departments have processEndOfDay(). Trading says close all open positions. Compliance says generate regulatory report. If Rajesh inherits both, which one does he follow? Ambiguous. Java prevents this by saying you can only belong to one department (single class inheritance). But you can hold multiple licenses (interfaces): Trading License and Compliance License. Rajesh implements both, and he decides how to do each one.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  DIAMOND PROBLEM (disallowed)
       Vehicle
      /       \
  Electric   Gas
      \       /
      Hybrid        <- AMBIGUOUS: which start()?

  JAVA SOLUTION (interfaces)
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  │ TradingService                │
  │   implements Tradable,        │
  │              Reportable       │
  │                               │
  │ Both have getMarket() default │
  │ Class MUST override:          │
  │   Tradable.super.getMarket()  │
  │   Reportable.super.getMarket()│
  │   or own implementation       │
  └──────────────────────────────┘

  Resolution priority:
  1. Class method (always wins)
  2. Sub-interface default
  3. Super-interface default
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Java disallows multiple class inheritance to prevent the diamond problem: if two parent classes both override the same method, the compiler cannot decide which version the child inherits. Java allows multiple interface implementation instead. If two interfaces have abstract methods with the same signature, the class provides one implementation satisfying both. If two interfaces have conflicting default methods, the compiler forces the class to override and explicitly resolve the conflict using InterfaceName.super.method() syntax.

The resolution priority is: class method always wins over interface defaults, sub-interface default wins over super-interface default, and two unrelated interface defaults require the implementing class to override.

Remember one sentence: Java prevents the diamond problem by disallowing multiple class inheritance and requiring the implementing class to explicitly resolve any conflicting interface default methods.
